clue.text: Small wound up carpet unravels

indicators.note: something that unravels comes apart and is remade, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rug coming apart at the seams after being rolled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small wound up' reads as a phrase about something tightly rolled; 'wound' is the injury, and 'up carpet' is the anagram material.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper slice on a finger is the classic tiny injury, a shallow cut from an edge of a sheet.

clue.text: Literary type charges Kindle outside

indicators.note: one piece is placed outside the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: to pique is to arouse or kindle interest
cares are people in one's charge, wards

explanation.surface: An e-reader as a literary gadget, with charges outside its case.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle, the e-reader brand, suggests books; here it is the verb to stir up.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of episodic novel following a roguish hero, such as Don Quixote or Tom Jones.

clue.text: Only women admitted into mobile phone event

indicators.note: something admitted into another is let inside it
mobile means moving freely, so the letters of the word phone are shifted about

parts.note: only women means no men, joined as one run

explanation.surface: A women-only event promoted by mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile phone' looks like a single object, but 'mobile' is the anagram signal, making PHEON; 'Only women' means no men at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable occurrence or happening is a phenomenon, any observable event.

clue.text: Show survey to the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the spelling follows what is heard

parts.note: a review is a survey or overview

explanation.surface: A theatre show polling its own audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A light theatrical entertainment of sketches, songs and dances is a type of show.

clue.text: Disorder precipitated when controls removed

parts.note: unrest is public disorder or disturbance
precipitation is rain, so precipitated means rained

explanation.surface: Riots broke out when curbs were lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitated' reads as caused; it is the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of any checks or curbs, so uncontrolled, the state left when restraints go.

clue.text: Probationer with a month to kill

parts.note: Nov is the standard abbreviation for November
to ice someone is slang for to kill them

explanation.surface: A trainee on probation given a month in which to carry out a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner admitted on trial, such as a monk before vows, is a probationer.

clue.text: Fine to repeat old clue about diamonds

indicators.note: the pair goes about, around, the suit letter, which sits between them
to repeat means say again, so the old clue appears twice

parts.note: a key is a clue to a puzzle
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Permission to reuse an old crossword clue about diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty colloquial way of saying all right or agreed.

clue.text: Fancy a fish first?

indicators.note: the fish comes first, placed in front of the letter a

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called orfe

explanation.surface: An offer of a fish course first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as would you like; it is the noun for a notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or whim, a thought in the mind.

clue.text: Spielberg's part for Hamburg banker

indicators.note: part of a word is some of its letters, so the answer is a run inside Spielberg's

explanation.surface: A film role for a German financier in a Spielberg movie.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, which has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The river that flows through Hamburg to the North Sea has banks, so it is a banker.

clue.text: Caught several out preparing joints with these

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of the word several are rearranged

explanation.surface: Several batsmen dismissed caught, read like a cricket score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' in a cricket scene looks like a dismissal, but it signals rearranging SEVERAL into LEAVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers' choppers are the heavy knives used to cut meat into joints.

clue.text: Sound effect always found in R&B

indicators.note: a word found in something sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: R&B, rhythm and blues, gives the letters R and B
ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A recording note that a certain studio sound always crops up in rhythm and blues.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverberation, the echo added to recordings, is a standard studio sound effect.

clue.text: Star spotters report reveals incorporation of US video system

indicators.note: incorporation means taking something into a body, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: a tale is an account or report
outs means exposes or reveals
NTSC is the American analogue television colour standard

explanation.surface: A report that celebrity spotters have taken up an American video format.
explanation.definitionFit: Recruiters looking for gifted performers or players spot future stars.

clue.text: State radio led with NHS reforms

indicators.note: reforms means remakes or reshapes, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: News that a radio campaign led the way in overhauling the health service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service; 'reforms' looks like its policy changes but rearranges RADIOLEDNHS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the smallest of the fifty US states, in New England.

clue.text: Relishes crunching second mint

indicators.note: crunching breaks something up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys crunching a second mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relishes' looks like a verb, enjoys; it is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauces, pickles and seasonings that add flavour to food are relishes.

clue.text: Litter mounts up after English Proms

indicators.note: the rest is placed after the English abbreviation
in a down entry up means reading from the bottom, so these pieces are reversed

parts.note: a sedan chair is a litter carried on poles
the Alps are mountains

explanation.surface: Rubbish piling up after an English concert season.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London concert series; here proms is short for promenades.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside walkways are promenades, called proms in British English.

clue.text: Woman left loud bar

parts.note: she is the pronoun standing for a woman
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A woman walked out of a noisy pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub and 'left' an exit; here bar is a ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge or rail fixed to a wall to hold things, a bar for books.

clue.text: Be first to compound effect of exposure

indicators.note: to compound is to mix together, so these letters are combined into a new order

explanation.surface: Urging someone to be the first to make things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' reads as worsen; it mixes BEFIRSTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue damaged by freezing is a result of exposure to cold.

clue.text: Impressive thing about iron-backed fasteners

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the whole built word is read in reverse
about means around, so the impressive thing goes round the metal

parts.note: a stonker is British slang for something hugely impressive
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A boast about strong fasteners with an iron back plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron-backed' reads as one adjective, but 'backed' turns STONKFEER (made by 'about') round. A stonker is British slang for a cracker.
explanation.definitionFit: Square knots joining two ropes are fastenings, used by sailors to tie reefs in sails.

clue.text: One working in hospital uniform given sweet substance

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Rolo is a brand of chocolate-covered caramel sweet
gist means the substance or essence of something

explanation.surface: A hospital worker in uniform handed a sticky sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet substance' looks like sugar; it splits into a sweet and a substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor specialising in the urinary tract works in a hospital department.

clue.text: Sing at the top of one's range?

definitions.text: Sing at the top of one's range?

parts.words: Sing at the top of one's range?
parts.note: a singer's range is their compass of notes, but a mountain range has peaks where Alpine singers call out

explanation.definitionFit: The warbling Alpine song style is sung among mountain peaks, the top of a range.

clue.text: Pit queen against king for the title of "hearty eater"

parts.note: a trench is a pit or ditch
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for the queen
a man is a playing piece in chess or draughts, and a draughts man crowned becomes a king

explanation.surface: Pitting a queen against a king in a contest for a title, like a chess match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit' and 'against' suggest a contest; pit is just TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher was a wooden platter, so a person who clears one is a big, hearty eater.

clue.text: Nurse given money owed to invest with

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
dues are what is owed, so due is money owed

explanation.surface: A nurse given back pay to put into investments.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone with a quality or garment, to furnish or clothe.

clue.text: See 23
Links warning to players' prediction

parts.note: golfers on the links shout fore to warn of a flying ball
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A golfer's shout leading into the players' predictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction, as of weather.

clue.text: Relaxed after a pick-me-up

parts.note: a tonic is a restorative drink or medicine, a pick-me-up

explanation.surface: Feeling relaxed after a restorative drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking muscle tone, so slack or unstressed, as in an unstressed syllable or a slack muscle.

clue.text: Return to club across narrow valley, carrying a heavy load

indicators.note: one piece goes across the other, spanning it, so it wraps round it
return means send back, so the word for club is read backwards

parts.note: to drub is to beat, as with a club
a dene is a narrow wooded valley

explanation.surface: A walker heading back to the club over a narrow valley with a heavy pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a noun but is the verb to beat; 'Return' turns it to BURD. A dene is a northern English word for a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weighed down with a heavy weight is laden, loaded or encumbered.

clue.text: Popular holiday destination involving a particular activity

definitions.meaning: split as two words, the Mediterranean, shortened, is a favourite place for sunny holidays
describing an event or venue organised round one subject, as a fancy-dress party

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it names the Mediterranean; whole, it describes a party built on one topic.

clue.text: Provides rating for a ship before winding turns

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard prefix for a ship
esses are S-shaped bends in a road

explanation.surface: A ship's rating given before it negotiates twisting bends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' suggests a naval sailor, fitting the ship; it means evaluation.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate something is to give it a rating or valuation.
